title: Leaving Berklee and joining Stevie Wonder
summary: Stevie Wonder came before Ellington; Baron left Berklee, joined Wonder's horn section and played on Music of My Mind.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: But what’s the biggest — was there a big difference from going to Duke Ellington to Stevie Wonder.
Stevie Wonder was before Duke Ellington. Wow.

Yeah. I was in Berklee School of Music in my fifth semester there. And everything started not making sense. There were too many rules. I told you, I was a rebel. You’d walk into some kind of composition class or something, and there were like twenty rules: you can’t do this, you can’t do this, can’t do this, and it was like man, this is not for me anymore. Music is not about rules, it’s about heart and soul and music. And so I left school. I had played with Stevie a couple of times when he was in town and he’d hire horn section and had a conductor, Gene Keefe, great guy. And he stayed on conducting when I joined the band for a while. And he was like one of these great supporters of me when I got the gig with Duke and stuff, he was like just thrilled, you know we stayed in touch for years. So when Stevie wanted to carry the whole thing instead of hiring horns, he liked the horns from Boston so he came to Boston and they hired horns. However, I didn’t make all the gigs, there was this other trombone player, this young red-haired guy named Kenny, and they asked him to do the tour and I was like oh, man. So I went to the trumpet player they had hired and I said, “Look, you know, if you ever need it, I’d love to come on.” And a couple of days later he calls me and said Kenny’s mother wouldn’t let him go on the road.

So and that was like a year and a half or so it went on. We went to South America and Europe, and it was so great. Talk about interviews, we had this one interview about Stevie. Stevie was just coming out of — actually I’ll just skip to this first — Stevie was just coming out of the “Fingertips,” “My Cherie Amour,” and into the new stuff, I’m on the album called “Music of My Mind” have you ever heard of that? And that was the first time he produced the whole album. He played everything except for me and Buzzy Feiten played guitar and he had a solo on this thing called “Love Havin’ You Around.”[sings] So he produced the whole thing. He was playing everything. And it was so funky and so great. And there’s a part where I have a solo and it’s of course everything but the kitchen sink in there so it comes in and out. But oh yeah, so Stevie had a thing that he used to do — is that what I was talking about —
